description: Gap 1 — Role-scope the main /dashboard. getDashboardData currently takes only a date range and returns org-wide hiring data to everyone who reaches the URL. Extend it to accept a session/user context and return one of three views (org-wide for admin/hr, team for managers, personal for employees), then render conditionally in DashboardPage, add an explicit auth route guard, and show the dashboard nav affordance to all authenticated roles. The 3-tier pattern to copy is in src/features/pulse/analytics/components/LeadershipDashboard.tsx (can(role,'manage_system')=org, can(role,'manage_one_on_ones')=team, else personal).
steps: 1. In src/features/dashboard/data.ts: change getDashboardData(range) to getDashboardData(range, ctx) with ctx = { userId: string; role: UserRole; department: string | null }. Import can from @/lib/rbac and UserRole from @/types/database. Add to DashboardData interface: view: 'org' | 'team' | 'personal'; and optional personal?: { recognitionsGiven: number; recognitionsReceived: number; goals: { onTrack: number; atRisk: number; completed: number; notStarted: number; total: number }; upcomingOneOnOnes: { id: string; scheduled_at: string; with: string }[]; pendingCheckin: boolean }. Compute view = can(role,'manage_system') ? 'org' : can(role,'manage_one_on_ones') ? 'team' : 'personal'. Bump cache key to cacheKey('dashboard','v4', `${rangeKey(range)}_${view}_${ctx.userId}`).

2. Still in data.ts — org branch: keep all existing queries unchanged (current behavior). team branch (manager): first fetch jobIds = (await supabaseAdmin.from('jobs').select('id').eq('department', ctx.department)).data mapped to id array; then filter every candidate-derived query (rangeCandidates, currentCandidates, scorecards via candidate_id) with .in('job_id', jobIds) when jobIds is non-empty (empty jobIds ⇒ empty candidate results); filter employees query with .eq('manager_id', ctx.userId) (covers activeEmployees count and newHires); fetch directReportIds = users where manager_id=ctx.userId, then filter checkins/goals with .in('user_id'|'owner_id', directReportIds); filter one_on_ones with .eq('manager_id', ctx.userId); filter scheduledJobs to department jobs (.in('id', jobIds)). The 'Employees' KPI = direct-report count for team view. Keep the rest of the aggregation logic identical.

3. Still in data.ts — personal branch (regular employee): return empty arrays/zeros for all hiring fields (stats.openJobs/activePipeline/pendingScreen/hired=0, pipeline=[], trend=[], rolePipeline=[], stageAging=[], recent=[], operations.interviewQueue=[], operations.scheduledJobs=[], operations.newHires=[], operations.activeSurveys=[], operations.health zeroed, operations.teamPulseTrend=[]). Fetch the user's own data: own goals (supabaseAdmin.from('goals').select('id,status,owner_id').eq('owner_id', ctx.userId)) → goals breakdown + total; own upcoming 1-on-1s (.from('one_on_ones').select('id, scheduled_at, manager:users!one_on_ones_manager_id_fkey(name)').eq('report_id', ctx.userId).gte('scheduled_at', now).order('scheduled_at').limit(5)) → map to {id, scheduled_at, with: manager.name}; own pending check-in for the current week (.from('checkins').select('status').eq('user_id', ctx.userId).eq('week_start', weekStart) → pendingCheckin = no submitted/reviewed row); recognitionsGiven = (await supabaseAdmin.from('feedback').select('id',{count:'exact',head:true})).eq('from_user_id', ctx.userId)).count ?? 0; recognitionsReceived = (await supabaseAdmin.from('feedback_recipients').select('user_id').eq('user_id', ctx.userId)).data?.length ?? 0. Build operations.actionItems from own pending check-in (label 'Your weekly check-in is due', tone amber, /pulse/checkins) and own at-risk goals (label 'Goals at risk', tone red, /pulse/goals), filtered to count>0. Populate data.personal and set data.view='personal'.

4. In src/features/dashboard/components/DashboardPage.tsx: call getDashboardData(range, { userId: session.user.id, role: session.user.role, department: session.user.department ?? null }). Branch on data.view === 'personal' → render a personal layout: keep the hero banner (greeting/role/department) but drop the 'awaiting AI screen' Link; render a 4-card KPI row from data.personal (Recognitions given → /pulse/feedback, Recognitions received → /pulse/feedback, Goals on track → /pulse/goals, Upcoming 1-on-1s → /pulse/one-on-ones) reusing the KpiCard component; render a row with 'My action items' (operations.actionItems), the existing GoalsWidget (onTrack/atRisk/completed/notStarted from data.personal.goals), and the 'Upcoming 1-on-1s' card (from data.personal.upcomingOneOnOnes, using report = with). Hide the interview queue, org team-pulse, pipeline funnel, top roles, DashboardCharts, HiringHealthChart, OfferTrackerChart, role schedule, new hires, active surveys sections. For 'org' and 'team' keep the existing JSX exactly as-is (team just receives scoped data). Update the DashboardHeader description for personal to something like `${recognitionsGiven} recognition${...} · ${goals.onTrack} goals on track`.

5. In src/app/(app)/dashboard/page.tsx: convert to an async default export that calls const session = await getServerSession(authOptions); if (!session) redirect('/login'); then return <DashboardPage />. Import getServerSession from next-auth, authOptions from @/lib/auth, redirect from next/navigation.

6. In src/lib/nav.ts navigationForRole: change the Home group so /dashboard is always shown (remove the `item.href !== '/dashboard' || isManager` condition) while keeping /staff gated to isManager. Resulting filter: group.items.filter((item) => item.href !== '/staff' || isManager).
acceptance_criteria: getDashboardData compiles with the new (range, ctx) signature and a view field on the returned object

An admin or HR user sees the unchanged org-wide dashboard; a manager sees only candidates/jobs in their department and only their direct reports in staff/pulse widgets; a regular employee sees the personal view with recognitions, goals, and 1-on-1s and no hiring pipeline
The Dashboard nav item is visible to all authenticated roles in navigationForRole
`npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run lint` are clean
verification: npm run lint  (expect no errors in the changed files)
